// Generated from the Erbium showcase catalog and shared Markdown. import { ShowcaseProviders, ShowcaseSurface } from "../preview"; import type { Meta, StoryObj } from "@storybook/react"; import { Sidebar } from "@/registry/erbium/ui/sidebar"; import PlaygroundExample, { defaultProps as PlaygroundDefaults } from "./variants/playground"; import OverviewExample from "./variants/overview"; const meta = { component: Sidebar, parameters: { docs: { description: { component: "## Usage Compose, theme, and customize a sidebar for your application. **Import:** `@/registry/erbium/ui/sidebar` ## Usage ```tsx import { SidebarProvider, SidebarTrigger } from "@/registry/erbium/ui/sidebar"; import { AppSidebar } from "@/components/app-sidebar"; export default function Layout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) { return (
{children}
); } ``` ```tsx import { Sidebar, SidebarContent, SidebarFooter, SidebarGroup, SidebarHeader, } from "@/registry/erbium/ui/sidebar"; export function AppSidebar() { return ( ); } ``` ## Links `SidebarMenuButton` and `SidebarMenuSubButton` take TanStack Router's link options. With `to` a row is a router link: `to`, `params`, `search`, `hash`, and `activeOptions` type against your routes, the route preloads before the click, and Router marks the current page with `aria-current="page"`, which applies the active styling. `href` takes a fully built or external URL. Without either, the row is a button. ```tsx import { SidebarMenuButton } from "@/registry/erbium/ui/sidebar"; Project GitHub New project ``` ## Composition Use the following composition to build a `Sidebar` layout: ```text SidebarProvider ├── Sidebar │ ├── SidebarHeader │ ├── SidebarContent │ │ ├── SidebarGroup │ │ │ ├── SidebarGroupLabel │ │ │ ├── SidebarGroupAction │ │ │ ├── SidebarGroupContent │ │ │ └── SidebarMenu │ │ │ ├── SidebarMenuItem │ │ │ │ ├── SidebarMenuButton │ │ │ │ ├── SidebarMenuAction │ │ │ │ └── SidebarMenuBadge │ │ │ └── SidebarMenuItem │ │ │ ├── SidebarMenuButton │ │ │ └── SidebarMenuSub │ │ │ ├── SidebarMenuSubItem │ │ │ └── SidebarMenuSubItem │ │ └── SidebarGroup │ │ └── SidebarMenu │ │ ├── SidebarMenuItem │ │ └── SidebarMenuItem │ ├── SidebarFooter │ └── SidebarRail ├── SidebarInset └── SidebarTrigger ``` ## Structure - **SidebarProvider** — Handles collapsible state and provides sidebar context to child components. - **Sidebar** — The main collapsible sidebar panel. - **SidebarHeader** — Sticky at the top; use for branding, titles, or workspace switchers. - **SidebarFooter** — Sticky at the bottom; use for user menus, settings, or actions. - **SidebarContent** — Scrollable region between the header and footer. - **SidebarGroup** — Groups related navigation with optional label, action, and content areas. - **SidebarMenu** / **SidebarMenuItem** — Menu structure for links, badges, actions, and nested submenus. - **SidebarRail** — Resize handle for adjusting sidebar width when applicable. - **SidebarInset** — Wraps main content when using the `inset` variant. - **SidebarTrigger** — Control that toggles the sidebar open or collapsed. ## SidebarProvider The `SidebarProvider` component is used to provide the sidebar context to the `Sidebar` component. You should always wrap your application in a `SidebarProvider` component. | Name | Type | Description | | --------------- | -------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | Default open state of the sidebar. | | `open` | `boolean` | Open state of the sidebar (controlled). | | `onOpenChange` | `(open: boolean) => void` | Sets open state of the sidebar (controlled). | | `defaultWidth` | `number` | Initial width in pixels. Unset, the width comes from `--sidebar-width`. | | `width` | `number` | Width in pixels (controlled). `undefined` falls back to `--sidebar-width`. | | `onWidthChange` | `(width: number \| undefined) => void` | Called when the rail resizes the sidebar (controlled). | | `minWidth` | `number` | Smallest width the rail resizes to. Defaults to 224. | | `maxWidth` | `number` | Largest width the rail resizes to. Defaults to 352. | Pass `open` and `onOpenChange` to control the sidebar: ```tsx const [open, setOpen] = React.useState(false); ; ``` `SidebarProvider` sets `--sidebar-width` (16rem) and `--sidebar-width-icon` (3rem) as classes. Override either one with a class on the provider; `cn` keeps the last value. The mobile sheet uses 18rem. To toggle the sidebar, `SidebarProvider` registers the `Mod+B` shortcut through TanStack Hotkeys — `Cmd+B` on macOS and `Ctrl+B` on Windows and Linux. ```tsx ``` ```tsx const SIDEBAR_KEYBOARD_SHORTCUT = "Mod+B"; ``` The provider wires the shortcut up with `useHotkey` from `@tanstack/react-hotkeys`, so the binding adapts to the platform and cleans itself up on unmount. `SidebarTrigger` announces it with `aria-keyshortcuts` and shows a hint badge while the user holds the modifier. The shortcut pauses while a modal dialog or sheet is open. ## Sidebar The main `Sidebar` component used to render a collapsible sidebar. | Property | Type | Description | | ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------- | | `side` | `left` or `right` | The side of the sidebar. | | `variant` | `sidebar` or `inset` | The variant of the sidebar. | | `collapsible` | `offcanvas`, `icon`, or `none` | Collapsible state of the sidebar. | | Prop | Description | | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | | `offcanvas` | A collapsible sidebar that slides in from the left or right. | | `icon` | A sidebar that collapses to icons. | | `none` | A non-collapsible sidebar. | **Note:** If you use the `inset` variant, remember to wrap your main content in a `SidebarInset` component. ```tsx
{children}
 ``` ## useSidebar The `useSidebar` hook is used to control the sidebar. | Property | Type | Description | | --------------- | ------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | | `state` | `expanded` or `collapsed` | The current state of the sidebar. | | `open` | `boolean` | Whether the sidebar is open. | | `setOpen` | `(open: boolean) => void` | Sets the open state of the sidebar. | | `openMobile` | `boolean` | Whether the sidebar is open on mobile. | | `setOpenMobile` | `(open: boolean) => void` | Sets the open state of the sidebar on mobile. | | `isMobile` | `boolean` | Whether the sidebar is on mobile. | | `toggleSidebar` | `() => void` | Toggles the sidebar. Desktop and mobile. | ```tsx import { useSidebar } from "@/registry/erbium/ui/sidebar"; export function AppSidebar() { const { state, open, setOpen, openMobile, setOpenMobile, isMobile, toggleSidebar } = useSidebar(); } ``` ## SidebarHeader Use the `SidebarHeader` component to add a sticky header to the sidebar. ```tsx }> Select Workspace Acme Inc ``` ## SidebarFooter Use the `SidebarFooter` component to add a sticky footer to the sidebar. ```tsx Username ``` ## SidebarContent The `SidebarContent` component is used to wrap the content of the sidebar. This is where you add your `SidebarGroup` components. It is scrollable. ```tsx ``` ## SidebarGroup Use the `SidebarGroup` component to create a section within the sidebar. A `SidebarGroup` has a `SidebarGroupLabel`, a `SidebarGroupContent` and an optional `SidebarGroupAction`. To make a `SidebarGroup` collapsible, wrap it in a `Collapsible`. ```tsx Application Add Project ``` ```tsx }> Help ``` ## SidebarMenu The `SidebarMenu` component is used for building a menu within a `SidebarGroup`. ```tsx {projects.map((project) => ( {project.name} ))} ``` ## SidebarMenuButton The `SidebarMenuButton` component is used to render a menu button within a `SidebarMenuItem`. It renders a button, or a router link when given `to` or `href` (see [Links](#links)). A row with `aria-current="page"` shows as active, which Router sets on the current page's link. ```tsx Home ``` ## SidebarMenuAction The `SidebarMenuAction` component is used to render a menu action within a `SidebarMenuItem`. ```tsx Home Add Project ``` ## SidebarMenuSub The `SidebarMenuSub` component is used to render a submenu within a `SidebarMenu`. ```tsx ``` ## SidebarMenuBadge The `SidebarMenuBadge` component is used to render a badge within a `SidebarMenuItem`. ```tsx 24 ``` ## SidebarMenuSkeleton The `SidebarMenuSkeleton` component is used to render a skeleton for a `SidebarMenu`. ```tsx {Array.from({ length: 5 }).map((_, index) => ( ))} ``` ## SidebarTrigger Use the `SidebarTrigger` component to render a button that toggles the sidebar. ```tsx import { useSidebar } from "@/registry/erbium/ui/sidebar"; export function CustomTrigger() { const { toggleSidebar } = useSidebar(); return ; } ``` ## Motion Opening and closing slides the sidebar over `duration-panel` (300ms) on `ease-ui-out`, `cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1)`, which starts fast and settles without a linear tail. With the `inset` variant the content surface moves its leading margin on the same curve, so it lands with the sidebar instead of snapping at the end. The mobile drawer uses `ease-ui-drawer`. All of it turns off under `prefers-reduced-motion`. ## SidebarRail `SidebarRail` is the sidebar's edge. Drag it to resize the sidebar between `minWidth` and `maxWidth`; dragging past half the minimum collapses it, and dragging a collapsed sidebar's edge opens it again. A click toggles the sidebar. The rail is a focusable window splitter: the arrow keys resize it (Shift moves further), Home and End jump to the bounds, and Enter toggles the sidebar. Leave the rail out for a sidebar that should not resize. While a drag is in progress the provider's wrapper carries `data-resizing`, which turns off the width transitions. The new width reaches `onWidthChange` when the pointer is released. ```tsx ``` ## Theming The sidebar uses its own CSS variables, defined for light and dark themes in `@erbium/ui/globals.css`. Override them to theme the sidebar separately from the rest of the app. | Variable | Use | | ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------- | | `--sidebar` | Sidebar background. | | `--sidebar-foreground` | Default text and icon color. | | `--sidebar-primary` | Emphasized content you add, such as a logo. | | `--sidebar-primary-foreground` | Text on `--sidebar-primary`. | | `--sidebar-accent` | Hover and active menu item background. | | `--sidebar-accent-foreground` | Text on `--sidebar-accent`. | | `--sidebar-border` | Borders and separators. | | `--sidebar-ring` | Focus ring. | ## Styling Here are some tips for styling the sidebar based on different states. ```tsx ``` ```tsx ``` ## Direction Use `DirectionProvider` and the matching HTML `dir` attribute for RTL layouts. Set `side="right"` to position the sidebar on the right. ## Base UI documentation Explore the underlying primitives and their API reference. - [Button](https://base-ui.com/react/components/button) - [mergeProps](https://base-ui.com/react/utils/merge-props) - [useRender](https://base-ui.com/react/utils/use-render) ## Keyboard shortcuts `SidebarProvider` registers its `Mod+B` toggle with TanStack Hotkeys, and `SidebarTrigger` reveals it with `KbdHint`. - [TanStack Hotkeys](https://tanstack.com/hotkeys/latest/docs/reference) - [useHotkey](https://tanstack.com/hotkeys/latest/docs/framework/react/reference/functions/useHotkey)", }, }, layout: "padded", }, tags: ["autodocs"], } satisfies Meta;
